Between Representation and Authentication
Female allegory and legal authority in the France–Brazil circulation, 1822–1906
Ana Vanzin
PhD candidate, PPGD/UFSC · Ius Gentium research group
Florianópolis, 13 November 2026
A Frenchwoman at the foot of the stairs
Hall of the Palácio do Governo, Desterro/Florianópolis, with the three busts. IHGSC, IHG-FOT-2460.
Marianne, Europa, América. Cast busts, Fonderies du Val d’Osne, Paris, 19th c.; Europa and América after models by Mathurin Moreaux (MHSC catalogue, 2023).
Ceiling stucco. Hermes with talaria, petasos and caduceus; a probable Tyche on a winged wheel; a child of abundance, Plutus (Malossi; Bononi, 2026).
Catalogue attribution. The museum attributes Marianne to Val d’Osne. How the bust was acquired remains unverified.
A reading, to be held as interpretation: the Republic seated between Europe and America, under commerce and fortune.
Ana Vanzin · Between Representation and Authentication
2
The question
When a female allegory represents the authority of the State, does she also authenticate it?
Working proposition
Representation and legal authority are distinct. The coin case shows why material resemblance alone cannot establish lawful manufacture.
France–Brazil circulation, in three material registers
I
Grammar
Ripa’s Iconologia travels as a manual. Debret, trained in Davidian neoclassicism, works inside that tradition.
II
Training
Décio Villares studies with Cabanel and shows at the 1874 Paris Salon. He contributes to the flag design in 1889. The dating of his Republic painting remains open.
III
Body and matter
Marianne enters the palace as sculpture. Bank statutes of December 1890 permit specified French gold coins as backing for note issue.
Ana Vanzin · Between Representation and Authentication
4
Four analytical functions
1
Representation
The figure stands for the polity.
2
Legitimation
The figure may lend the order dignity or help secure consent.
3
Authentication
A legal criterion certifies that an object or act is genuine.
4
Justification
The order is applied as law.
These functions are not chronological stages. Today I ask how legitimation relates to legal authentication.

6
Zwischenraum, 1494–1603
Can a figure convey a norm without telling a story?
A woman can personify Justice without women holding the same legal positions. The comparison calls for evidence about particular institutions and periods.
Debret, 1822: the Constitution on stage before the Constitution
Debret, Voyage pittoresque, vol. III (1839), pl. 49: “Pano de boca … por ocasião da Coroação do imperador D. Pedro I”.
The surviving watercolour’s collection and dating still need verification.
1 Dec 1822. For the coronation of Pedro I, Debret paints the drop curtain of the court theatre.
Centre. A seated, crowned woman with the sword and the tablets of the Constitution: the Imperial Government.
Anticipation. The tablets are on stage before Brazil’s 1824 Constitution; the Charter comes in March 1824.
1839. Plate 49 brings the scene to French readers.
Correction: Rosa, Rodrigues and Abraham (2020, p. 71-72) read the centre as the emperor; Debret’s own description (Silva, 2017, p. 32; Lima Junior, 2020, p. 136-139) names the female personification.
Ana Vanzin · Between Representation and Authentication
8
December 1890
One month ties image, value and law
6 Dec
Decree 1.127
The Penal Code of 1890 enters into force in the Federal District on 20 Dec 1890; in Minas Gerais and the coastal states, on 1 Feb 1891.
7 Dec
Decree No. 1,154, arts. 1 and 3
Authorises the bank merger and permits note issue against a gold deposit.
30 Dec
Decree No. 1,227, annexed statutes
Article 10 allows French 10- and 20-franc gold coins to back note issue. Article 9 § 11 addresses counterfeit notes.
Eligibility as backing does not itself establish general legal tender or actual circulation.
Ana Vanzin · Between Representation and Authentication
9
[Image pending] 20 francs gold, Génie type
Génie type, associated with Augustin Dupré. The specimen and its inscription still need verification.
Penal Code 1890, art. 239: moeda falsa
“Fabricar, sem autoridade legitima, moeda feita de identica materia, com a mesma forma, peso e valor intrinseco da verdadeira”
[Translation] “To manufacture, without lawful authority, a coin of identical material, with the same form, weight and intrinsic value as the genuine coin.”
Even a materially identical copy could be counterfeit if made without lawful authority.
Open question. The sole paragraph punishes coin made “com diversa materia ou sem o peso legal” more heavily: 2 to 8 years, against 1 to 4 for the perfect copy. Why does the imperfect imitation weigh more?
Back to the stairs: different uses of images
Seals: abstraction
Decree No. 4 (1889) specifies non-anthropomorphic symbols. What makes a seal legally effective depends on the rules for its use.
Coin and palace: a body
1906: the 1000 réis coin with the Effigy of the Republic (BR-1000R-1906), a white, European-featured profile.
Visual Sexual Contract
The figure represents the polity; that does not show who held political or civil rights. National suffrage was recognised in 1932. The 1916 Civil Code took effect in 1917.

11
How this argument could fail
1
If figures of another gender work the same way, femininity is not indispensable to that function.
2
Appropriation of the allegory accompanied by effective legal inclusion of women.
3
Indicators of the hardening of images that vary independently of legal practice.
In a fragmentary corpus, archival silence counts as a mechanism not yet demonstrated, and only as that.
When does an image become part of a legally authorised object or act? What procedure would show it?
